title: Logistics Standard: Shipment, Branch Delivery and Closure of Factory Production Orders
content:
**Standard.** The order ships when its last unit leaves the factory and is expected at the branch within the class transit time. The branch inspects delivered units within the inspection window; freight damage found in that window is remade as freight damage at no charge. Branch delivery opens the installation job for the order. The order closes when the installation job for its contract is completed. An order that has shipped cannot be cancelled; if its contract is cancelled after shipment the units stay on the order and the contract's cancellation terms carry their cost.

This standard applies to all Factory Production Orders; the transit time and the inspection window are figures of the order's build class.

## Stages after the factory

| Stage | What marks it | What follows |
|---|---|---|
| Shipped | the last unit of the order leaves the factory | expected at the branch within the class transit time |
| Delivered | the order is received at the Ridgeline branch warehouse | the branch inspects within the inspection window; the installation job for the order is opened |
| Closed | the installation job for the order's contract is completed | — |

## Freight damage

Freight damage found by the branch inside the inspection window is remade with the cause freight damage and carries no charge to the customer.

## Contract cancelled after shipment

A shipped or delivered order is not cancelled. When the contract is cancelled after shipment, the units stay on the order, and what the cancellation costs the customer is decided by the contract's own cancellation terms.

## Hypothetical example

A Specialty Shape Build order (transit of 3 business days) ships its last unit on a Tuesday with no federal holiday that week; it is expected at the branch on the Friday. Its first units shipped the week before do not change the ship date, which is the Tuesday.
